title: Human-AI Teaming Through the Lens of Calibration
abstract: arXiv:2606.10906v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: We study models for human-AI teaming through the lens of statistical calibration. We assume the team consists of an AI model and human---both of which are calibrated with respect to some partitioning of the feature space---and expose how the calibration assumptions propagate into the teaming framework. In particular, we consider frameworks that either (i) combine human and model predictions or (ii) delegate prediction responsibility to either a human or model. We show via theoretical and empirical results that existing methods for combination do not preserve the human's degree of calibration. Methods for delegation (by the very act of delegation) preserve calibration of the downstream predictors but shift the burden onto the rejector meta-model that decides who predicts. The rejector must be calibrated finely enough to locate where each member is superior, a demand that grows with the human's expertise and becomes unattainable

translated_title: 通过校准视角审视人机协作团队
translated_abstract: 我们通过统计校准的视角研究人机协作团队的模型。我们假设团队由一个AI模型和一个人类组成——两者均相对于特征空间的某种划分是经过校准的——并揭示校准假设如何传播到协作框架中。特别地，我们考虑两类框架：(i) 组合人类和模型的预测，或 (ii) 将预测责任委托给人类或模型。我们通过理论和实证结果表明，现有的组合方法无法保持人类的校准程度。而委托方法（正是由于委托这一行为本身）能够保持下游预测器的校准，但会将负担转移到决定由谁进行预测的拒绝元模型上。该拒绝模型必须经过足够精细的校准，才能定位每个团队成员更具优势的区域，而这一要求会随着人类专业水平的提升而增长，最终变得难以实现。
tldr: 本文从统计校准视角分析人机协作团队框架，发现组合人类与模型预测的现有方法会破坏人类的校准性，而委托方法虽能保持校准，却将负担转移到需要精细校准且难以达到要求的拒绝元模型上。
en_tdlr: This paper analyzes human-AI teaming through the lens of statistical calibration, showing that existing combination methods fail to preserve human calibration, while delegation methods preserve it but shift the burden onto a rejector meta-model whose calibration demands become unattainable as human expertise grows.
